page_title: The Tail at Scale | bill duncan's blog

summary.name: The Tail at Scale (SLO math)
summary.one_liner: A blog post working through the probability math for setting back end latency SLOs when a request fans out to many back end systems, building on the "Tail at Scale" paper.
use_cases: derive back end SLO targets from a user-facing SLO
estimate required nines for a large service fanout
reason about tail latency in distributed systems
decide whether to send hedged or deferred replica requests
calculate combined success probability with bc
summary.what_it_does: The post explains how to derive back end latency objectives from a user-facing SLO when a request fans out to N back end systems. It gives the formula SLA = SLO^N for independent systems and shows worked examples: a 95% target across 50 systems needs about 3 nines (0.9990) per back end, and across 500 systems about 4 nines (0.99990), with the calculation done in bc -l. It includes a short probability refresher on union and intersection of failure events. A real Lucene index case study describes using deferred secondary requests to handle outliers, since most responses arrived within half the budget. The author notes that hedged requests would double traffic.
notable: Worked example deriving required per-backend nines from a 95% user SLO at 50 and 500 fanout
Real case study with thousands of Lucene index back end apps and a 20-second query SLO
Discusses deferring secondary requests to replicas instead of hedging to avoid doubling traffic
caveats: Explicitly does not cover user-level SLOs or SLAs
Assumes back end systems are independent and equal, which the author admits is rarely true
Presents the math as a rough estimate; the author concludes with 'Probably.'
